blocks.text: You studied the basics of Mendelian genetics in Grade X. This chapter carries the idea forward to the research done after Mendel, and it also looks at some inherited diseases, their symptoms and their treatment.

blocks.title: Recalling: true-breeding plants
blocks.text: The Austrian monk Gregor Johann Mendel was the first to explain the mechanism of inheritance. He developed true-breeding (pure-breeding) varieties of pea plants: a plant that is true-breeding for a trait gives offspring all with the same trait when it is self-fertilized.

Mendel made monohybrid crosses in pea plants. In the first he followed seed shape: when he crossed a true-breeding round-seeded plant with a wrinkled-seeded plant, all the plants of the F1 generation produced round seeds.

items: Dominant trait: the trait that is expressed in the F1 plants (round seeds).
Recessive trait: the alternative trait that is not expressed in the F1 plants (wrinkled seeds).
